rule.statement: A contract requires an offer and acceptance, and the intention to create a legal relationship and a consensus ad idem or meeting of the minds needs to be in existence to establish a contract.
rule.supporting_quote: It is an elementary rule that every contract requires an offer and acceptance. Therefore an offer or promise which is not accepted, is not actionable [vide Justice Weerasooriya in Muthukuda v. Sumanatwathie, (1962) 65 NLR 205, 208, 209]. It has been stated that it is an elementary proposition of law that a contract is concluded when in the mind of each contracting party there is a consensus ad idem.
